- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) within 5–7 days, model overconfidently holds high forecasts; apply downward bias of 1–3% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per negative sentiment day; if below, increase by 1% per positive sentiment day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply slight downward correction (0.5–1.5%) for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment flips from + to -, reduce slope).
